clue.text: Woollen garments prove best in test arranged

indicators.note: the words prove best are placed within the letters of test once those are rearranged
arranged tells us the letters of test are put into a new order

parts.note: to prove best is to win

explanation.surface: A knitwear trial in which jumpers are put through their paces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prove best' looks like part of the surface's trial, but it is the piece placed inside the rearranged letters that 'arranged' signals, giving TSET split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching cardigan and jumper in wool, sold together as a pair, is the classic twin set.

clue.text: Every one included in the list may be given instruction

indicators.note: included in means every one sits inside the list word

parts.note: a table is a list or chart
each means every one

explanation.surface: Anyone named on the roster can be trained.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone able to learn or be taught is fit to receive lessons.

clue.text: Earnings in the main come so regularly

indicators.note: in signals the answer is held inside the run of words the main come so

explanation.surface: Wages arrive dependably for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' is only surface padding: the run sits in maIN COME So, not in alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Money received from work or investments is what people earn.

clue.text: What's said to emanate from one's bank manager

definitions.text: to emanate from one's bank manager

explanation.surface: Wondering about the words a bank official is bound to come out with.
explanation.definitionFit: Something declared is an utterance; and a bank sends customers a periodic account summary.

clue.text: Mark needs only a moment

explanation.surface: A teacher's check symbol needs just a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A check mark on a list; and an instant, as in 'back in a jiffy'.

clue.text: The French entering the Civil Service — so exemplary

indicators.note: entering means the French article goes inside the abbreviation for the Civil Service

parts.note: CS is the standard abbreviation for the Civil Service
la is the feminine form of 'the' in French
sic is Latin for 'so, thus', used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A Frenchman joins the British Civil Service and proves a model employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exemplary serves as a model of its kind, just as a standard, archetypal work does.

clue.text: Branches with light tips

parts.note: sounds like a tree with pale twigs, but describes a holder whose arms each carry a candle flame

explanation.definitionFit: A large branched candlestick holds a flame at the end of each arm.

clue.text: Degree up — fuel making it very hot

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the degree is written bottom to top

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: The temperature rises as fuel is burned, making things scorching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degree' suggests temperature; it is the academic BA, turned to AB by 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling liquid is at its hottest, bubbling at full heat.

clue.text: Foreign holy man over the mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the saint above the mountains

parts.note: St, saint, is a holy man
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: An overseas monk crosses the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfamiliar or alien, as in being a stranger in a strange land.

clue.text: Plain net

explanation.surface: A two-word description of simple, unadorned fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious or evident; and to earn as profit after deductions.

clue.text: A couple of hundred gunmen altogether? That's capital!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two hundreds give CC
the RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British Army's gunners taken as a body

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at a band of two hundred armed men assembled at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'That's capital!' sounds like British praise, but capital is the definition: the city is Ghana's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: Meeting to study progress

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a course is a progress or onward movement, as in the course of events

explanation.surface: A gathering held to examine how things are advancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a coming together or assembly of people, a gathering.

clue.text: Arkwright's son allowed a title role

parts.note: Noah built the Ark, so he is jokingly an 'ark-wright'; Ham was one of his sons
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A family business heir is permitted to take the lead part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkwright looks like a surname (Richard Arkwright, the mill inventor), but here it means the builder of the Ark, Noah.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy is named after its Danish prince, so the character is a title part.

clue.text: A German will take ship after the latter part of October

indicators.note: after places the ship following the piece from October in the answer
only the latter part of the word October is kept, dropping its opening four letters

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A German plans to sail at the end of October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' lets the ship follow in the clue yet come second in the grid; 'latter part of' keeps the closing three letters of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is a native or inhabitant of Germany's capital city.

clue.text: Requiring settlement, call a court assessor

indicators.note: letters needing to be settled are unsettled, so call a court is rearranged

explanation.surface: A dispute needs resolving, so someone summons a judge to assess damages.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that works out sums and figures is something that assesses quantities.

clue.text: How to treat roasting meat — beat with a stick

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction that turns violent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooks spoon hot fat over a joint as it roasts; separately, an old verb means to thrash or cudgel someone.

clue.text: Room appropriate to take in painters for instance

indicators.note: to take in means the appropriate word surrounds the painters

parts.note: apt means appropriate or suitable
painters are examples of art men, men of art

explanation.surface: A space suitable for having the decorators in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painters' tempts the decorator sense; it means artists, ART MEN, set between A and PT of APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat or a single chamber in a building can both be called by this word, especially in American use.

clue.text: Brown is held by a relation to be provoking

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: held by means is sits inside the relation word

parts.note: a tale is a relation, a narrative told

explanation.surface: A sun-tanned relative is kept captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' points to a relative, but here it means an account or story told; 'held by' puts the little word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease by holding something desirable just out of reach is to provoke.

clue.text: Drink one at a time in playful mockery

parts.note: tea is a drink
singly means one at a time

explanation.surface: Sipping drinks one by one while being ribbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbing or joshing someone is done in a light, mocking spirit.

clue.text: Property conveyance?

parts.note: conveyance sounds like the legal transfer of property, but read as a vehicle belonging to a landed holding it is a kind of car

explanation.definitionFit: A family car with a long body and rear door; the word for a landed holding plus a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Dashes round Georgia with the means of quelling riots

indicators.note: round means the dashes word goes around Georgia

parts.note: tears are rushes or dashes, as in tearing along
GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Police rush around Georgia to put down unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashes' reads as punctuation; it means rushes, TEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use an irritant spray that makes the eyes stream to disperse crowds.

clue.text: Type article for a girl

parts.note: a norm is a standard type or pattern
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Picking out the right sort of word to put before a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female first name, as in Bellini's opera heroine.

clue.text: Among the others Islam's caliph is a practical type

indicators.note: among means the caliph is placed inside the others

parts.note: the rest means the others
Ali was the fourth caliph of Islam

explanation.surface: Of all the rulers, one Muslim leader stands out as pragmatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sees things as they are and acts sensibly is pragmatic.

clue.text: Long-legged type of weightlifter to travel by air

parts.note: a crane is a machine that hoists heavy loads
to fly is to travel by air

explanation.surface: A lanky athlete who lifts weights also takes plane trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weightlifter' conjures an athlete; it is the lifting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The daddy-long-legs is an insect with very long, thin legs.

clue.text: Turn into the Channel Islands to get plants

indicators.note: into means the turn goes inside the islands abbreviation

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off France's coast
an act is a turn, a performance on stage

explanation.surface: Steering towards Jersey and Guernsey for a gardening trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' suggests steering; it is a stage turn, ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny desert succulents are a family of plants.

clue.text: The monarch, right or wrong

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Asking whether the sovereign is correct or mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong, as a noun, is a mistake or fault.

clue.text: Is retired and occupied by a distant expedition

indicators.note: occupied by means the reversed word has the distant word inside it
retired means withdrawn, so the word is goes backwards

parts.note: afar means far away, distant

explanation.surface: A man in retirement goes off on a far-away trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' sounds like a pensioner but turns the two-letter word round to SI, which 'occupied by' splits open.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey into the wild, especially in Africa to see or hunt animals, is a kind of expedition.

clue.text: No end of danger for iolanthe

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter is cut from the danger word

parts.note: peril means danger

explanation.surface: Peril everywhere for the fairy heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Iolanthe is the fairy title character of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth a fairy or beautiful spirit; the opera's heroine is one such sprite.

clue.text: Mention about great rambling weed

indicators.note: about means the mention word goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: to cite is to mention or quote

indicators.note: rambling suggests wandering, so the letters of great are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a big overgrown plant in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' gives GARET, which 'about' places inside the mention word. 'weed' looks like a garden plant but is old slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco has long been called 'the weed', so a smoke rolled in paper fits.

clue.text: Topping cake!

parts.note: Topping cake! reads like an old-fashioned exclamation of delight, but describes the sugary layer spread over a cake

explanation.definitionFit: The sweet glaze or frosting put on top of a sponge is what the clue describes.

clue.text: One who accommodates one looking for cover

definitions.text: One who accommodates one looking for cover

parts.words: One who accommodates one looking for cover
parts.note: the picture is of someone giving shelter, but the cover sought is financial protection against loss, provided by a company

explanation.definitionFit: A company that sells policies provides protection against risk to customers seeking it.

clue.text: One quarter see about exercising in a clumsy way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N, north, is one quarter of the compass

indicators.note: about means the see is placed around the exercise letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in England
PT, physical training, means exercising

explanation.surface: Someone in a corner watches a person working out awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not a verb here but a diocese: Ely, an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without skill or deftness is doing it awkwardly.
